title: ha/dr: automate multi-AZ failover, restore drills, and runbooks-as-code (helm + terraform + installer)
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in regulated environments require tested, repeatable HA and DR procedures for multi-AZ setups. This PR automates failover and restore drills end-to-end and codifies runbooks so they can be executed by CI or runbooks-as-code tooling. Summary of changes: 1) Installer: add --ha-check and --drill subcommands that wire into the operator to trigger controlled failovers and cluster restores; include idempotent safety checks and dry-run option. 2) Helm charts: add chart hooks and readiness probes for HA failover (leader election annotations, pod disruption budgets tuned per AZ), introduce optional kafka/redis affinity changes for cross-AZ replication, new values: ha.enabled, ha.preferred_azs, ha.failover_policy. 3) Terraform modules: new module terraform/modules/ha with resources and null_resource-based runbook steps (uses local-exec to call installer/drill); outputs include runbook_url and last_run_timestamp. 4) Runbooks-as-code: add runbooks/ha-dr/runbooks.yaml templated descriptions for restore and failover drills, plus a small runner (scripts/runbook-runner.sh) used by CI. 5) Upgrade/rollback tooling: add a scripted canary/rollback hook to installer that can be invoked during upgrades and binds to Terraform outputs to determine candidate nodes. Safety: default ha.enabled=false; failover/drill require explicit confirmation or DRILL_TOKEN env var. Backwards compatibility: Helm values default to current behaviour when ha.enabled is not set. Checklist: - [x] Installer subcommand implementation and unit tests - [x] Helm chart changes + values docs - [x] Terraform module + examples - [x] Runbooks added and validated locally - [x] CI job to run a dry-run drill on PRs - [x] Docs updated in repo README and runbooks index How this was validated: ran an end-to-end dry-run in the staging multi-AZ cluster, executed a controlled leader failover and verified traffic moved within SLOs; executed a restore drill against a snapshot in a sandbox; ran the new terraform module example in ci/examples/ha and validated outputs. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable ha.enabled=true in an internal staging overlay for two weeks, run two scheduled restore drills, collect telemetry. After validation, enable on customer-facing example overlays and publish runbook docs. Rollback: installer supports --rollback-to <checkpoint> and terraform module exposes checkpoint outputs for quick rollback. Related Linear: ENG-4318, ENG-4321. Related Jira (support): SUP-2142. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the changes modular across installer/helm/terraform/runbooks to allow backporting pieces separately. Detailed diffs are small; heavy lifting is orchestration logic in installer and the templated runbooks.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can we make the default PDB tolerations less aggressive for small clusters? Suggested changing minAvailable to 1 for size < 3.
Aisha Kaur: Updated PDB template to compute minAvailable based on .Values.cluster.size; added unit test and note in chart docs.
Priya Nair: Please add a safety gate so drill cannot be executed against production overlay without DRILL_TOKEN.
Aisha Kaur: Added DRILL_TOKEN check and explicit confirmation prompt; documented in runbooks/ha-dr/README.md.
Connor Lee: CI dry-run failed in first run due to missing kubeconfig in runner; added fallback and clearer error messages.
Aisha Kaur: Fixed CI job and re-ran; green.
release_notes: Add optional HA/DR automation for private installer: multi-AZ failover, restore drills, runbooks-as-code, and terraform module. Disabled by default; see docs/ha-dr for enabling instructions.
how_tested: End-to-end dry-run in staging cluster, unit tests for installer and helm templates, terraform example apply in sandbox, CI dry-run job validates non-destructive behavior.
rollout_plan: Merge to main -> enable in internal staging overlay for 2 weeks -> run scheduled drills -> review telemetry -> enable in customer example overlays -> publish docs.
rollback_instructions: Use installer --rollback-to <checkpoint> or apply terraform module checkpoint outputs; run runbooks/runbooks.yaml restore flow. Emergency: set ha.enabled=false in overlay and scale down new failover hooks.
notes: This PR keeps ha features behind flags to allow incremental backports. The runbooks are intentionally templated to integrate with runbook-runner and can be executed by CI for scheduled drills.
